sections.title: The sound of au
paragraphs: The letters au make the sound /ɔː/. A vowel is a sound made with open air. You hear this long vowel in (author) /ɔː.θər/, which means a person who writes a book. These letters have three sounds in English speech.

sections.title: How to say au
paragraphs: For the first sound, pull your tongue back into the middle of the mouth. Make your lips into a circle. For the second sound, open your mouth wide. Drop your jaw low and pull your tongue back. For the third sound, open your mouth wide and round your lips lightly. Touch your throat to feel your voice shake on each sound.

sections.title: Spelling of au
paragraphs: Most often, these letters sound like /ɔː/ before a consonant, as in (pause) /pɔːz/. In a few words before nasal consonants or fricatives, they sound like /ɑː/, as in (aunt) /ɑːnt/. They make the short sound /ɒ/ in a few everyday words, such as (because) /bɪ.kɒz/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not read these letters as two separate vowel sounds. Do not say a diphthong like the vowel in house. Keep the sound steady and hold your tongue in one place.
